purpose: Controlled French voice-quality test after A_FR_v2 (Dubbing v2) was human-QA-failed for being too fast and not sufficiently native-sounding. Tests whether removing the forced-duration constraint and swapping to a native French Voice Library voice (no source-voice cloning) fixes both problems, independent of the $43/33 issue (not addressed here per instruction).

config_inspection.dubbing_v2_timing_behavior_found: Empirical evidence from the A_DE/A_FR/A_KO v2 builds: ElevenLabs Dubbing v2's 'automatic' mode returns an audio/video duration matching the ORIGINAL SOURCE VIDEO length regardless of the 'expected_duration_sec' estimate given at job submission (e.g. DE job estimated 70.08s at submit, actual returned duration was 57.54s = original video length). This confirms Dubbing v2 in automatic mode forces output timing to the source video's duration -- there is no documented parameter (start_time/end_time only trims input; no 'natural_pacing' or 'no_compress' flag exists in the API) to disable this. This is why this test switches to direct multilingual Text-to-Speech instead of Dubbing v2, per instruction.
config_inspection.disable_voice_cloning_param: Exists on the Dubbing v2 create endpoint (bool, default false). When true, Dubbing v2 substitutes a Voice Library voice instead of cloning the source speaker -- this is the lever for 'native delivery over source-voice similarity' within Dubbing v2 itself. NOT used in this test because Dubbing v2's timing behavior (above) is the dominant problem the human flagged (speech too fast), and disable_voice_cloning does not address timing. Recorded here for completeness/future reference.
config_inspection.target_accent_param: Exists on Dubbing v2 (experimental, influences voice selection + translation for a requested accent). Not used here since this test bypasses Dubbing v2 entirely.
config_inspection.decision: Used ElevenLabs standard multilingual Text-to-Speech (POST /v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}) with a native French Voice Library voice and our existing Gemini French translation text, with NO duration constraint of any kind.

source.selection_rationale: Same visible-speaking, no-cut, normal-conversational-claim segment used for the earlier A_DE 7s sample validation, chosen here again for cross-language/cross-test comparability.
source.french_text_used: Je sais, la plupart prennent une éternité. C'est pour ça que Freecash a 4,7 sur Trustpilot, et ils me paient le jour même, donc c'est du solide.
source.text_source: reports/A_FR_translation.json segments 7-9 (existing Gemini translation, reused verbatim, no new Gemini call made)

provider.name: ElevenLabs
provider.voice_source: ElevenLabs shared Voice Library (GET /v1/shared-voices?language=fr&gender=male), NOT a clone of the original English speaker -- source-voice cloning was not used at all for this test, maximizing native-delivery likelihood per instruction priority order.
provider.speed_parameter_used: none (omitted entirely -- no speed/duration control passed, output is the model's natural unconstrained pacing)

timing.note: French came out ~16% longer than the English source clip. The OUTPUT VIDEO was extended (not the audio shortened) via a deterministic freeze-hold on the last video frame (ffmpeg tpad clone, +1.13s), matching the project's existing hold-extension technique from the original Challenger A hook build. No audio speed/pitch alteration of any kind was applied.

output.captions: not added -- this is a voice-quality-only test per instruction scope (no caption/full-pipeline work requested).

perceptual_quality.note: Pronunciation/nativeness/cadence NOT auto-approved. This test changes two variables at once versus the failed A_FR_v2 (voice source: native library voice vs cloned; timing: unconstrained vs forced-to-video-length) -- if this sounds better, a follow-up could isolate which change mattered, but that is a decision for human review, not assumed here.
